data.narrative:
Red 6, a Series B+ defense and security company that has raised over $100M to date, presents a valuation challenge due to limited comparable data at its specific stage and tier. The broader defense and security sector includes 21 peer companies, of which 2 trade publicly (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 operate privately. However, no subset of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yields the minimum three datapoints required for reliable peer-median analysis, rendering traditional comps-based triangulation inapplicable.

The identified private peer universe—Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems—represents the most relevant benchmark set by business proximity, though stage and valuation tier heterogeneity within this group limits direct multiples application. The two public comparables (DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS) operate in adjacent defense markets but may not fully reflect the risk and growth profile of an early-stage private defense-tech company still scaling commercial traction.

Given these constraints, a valuation of Red 6 cannot be credibly anchored to peer multiples or median approaches. Analysis would require reliance on alternative methods—DCF modeling against management guidance, revenue growth rates, or margin trajectory assumptions—none of which are provided in the current dataset. The key uncertainty remains the absence of quantifiable operational metrics (revenue, runway, customer concentration, contract value) that would enable bottom-up valuation grounding.
